newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOOSNAM RISES ABOVE WENTWORTH WIND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM RISES ABOVE WENTWORTH WIND.

text.p: Ian Woosnam led a posse of Ryder Cup teammates by two shots after a four-under-par 68 in the second round of the British PGA Championship on Saturday.

Nick Faldo, David Gilford and Colin Montgomerie are all in hot pursuit of the Welshman, winner of the title in 1988, who defied a swirling wind to post a nine-under total of 135 over the 6,957-yard Wentworth course.

Faldo, the U.S.-based Englishman who has won this title four, carded a joint day's best of 67 to advance to seven under, level with quiet northern England cattle farmer Gilford, who shot an erratic 70.

Reigning European number one and world number six Montgomerie, who has never won at Wentworth, recorded his second three-under-par 69, helped by chip-ins for birdies at the 13th and 14th, but was disappointed not to birdie either of the last two par fives.
He was alone in fourth place on six under, one better than the best overseas players, Trinidad's Stephen Ames and Frank Nobilo of New Zealand who compiled rounds of 69 and 71 respectively.
The joint overnight leaders, Irishmen Darren Clarke and Eamonn Darcy, fell back with rounds of 74 and 75 and are on four under and three under par respectively.
South African Ernie Els was level with Clarke after a 71 but Bernhard Langer of Germany fell away with a 75 after his opening 67.
Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal shot 71 to stand on one under but his compatriot and Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros, who shot 76 on Friday, withdrew with a bad back before even starting his round.
The halfway cut fell at three over and the main casualties on four over were U.S.-based Swede Jesper Parnevik after a 78 and Zimbabwean Mark McNulty with his second 74.

Woosnam dropped shots at the second and third holes but then the shorter, 32-inch putter he is now using got hot. He birdied the fourth and ninth on putts of 15 and 20 feet and then collected further birdies at the 12th, 13th, 16th and 18th, the last from 15 feet again.
"I moved my hands a bit higher on the putter today and I seemed to have a little more control," he said.
He has also shortened his swing in recent weeks, giving him more control in the wind.
The heart of Faldo's fine round was a great 30-yard pitch into the 13th hole for a birdie.
He had three successive birdies from the second and another at the ninth, then three on the back nine along with two bogeys.
"My game is getting better," said Faldo, who missed successive halfway cuts at the Masters and MCI Classic events last month when his putting touch deserted him.
"My putting was a lot better today but there are a few funny shots to work on."
